subject: Re: Trial scope amendment — add real-time intent use case and revised acceptance metrics
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@tidalhealth.com>, integrations@tidalhealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-02-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: POC plan & acceptance criteria (post-call recap)

Jordan / team — thanks again for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have an agreed single source of truth. If anything below looks off, flag and I’ll update.

High-level POC objective
- Validate that Redwood can reliably serve TidalHealth’s intent routing for both conversational search and a new low-latency "real-time intent" path for live triage. Primary goals are reliability under expected load and demonstrable user-facing latency improvements.

Proposed success criteria (starting point)
- Conversational search: intent classification accuracy >= 92% on your labeled test set (batch evaluation)
- Real-time intent: 95th percentile latency <= 250 ms end-to-end (inference + network) for 90% of test sessions
- Throughput: sustain 50 requests/sec for peak slice with tail latencies within SLOs
- Quality guardrails: no more than 2% regression vs baseline on false-positive routing rate

Scope / deliverables
- Data ingest: you provide ~5k anonymized sample events + intent labels for the two target flows by 2027-02-05
- Deployment: hosted trial with a dedicated small GPU pool, model variants for low-latency path, and tracing enabled
- Eval package: we run scheduled evals against your test sets and provide token-level latency/cost breakdowns
- Timeline: start of trial provisioning week of 2027-02-07, nominal 4-week execution with one checkpoint at 2 weeks

Attachments: proposed-eval-matrix.xlsx (matrix of intents, metrics, and owners) and proposed-sow-v1.docx (POC SOW) — links below.

Open questions / asks for you
1) Can you confirm delivery of sample data by 2027-02-05?
2) Does your security team need a workspace-level SLA or additional docs before we provision a dedicated pool?
3) Are you okay with our default acceptance metric framing above, or do you want to tighten the real-time percentile?

Next steps
- Jordan to confirm data timeline and whether low-latency target should be tightened (reply here)
- We’ll pause provisioning until scope confirmed, but will hold an allocation tentative for week of 2/7
- Ben / Marissa: please review feasibility notes (Ben) and onboarding checklist (Marissa) and reply with capacity impacts by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0134

Thanks Kim — appreciate the clear recap. A couple clarifications from our side after chatting with the integrations team: 

1) We want to add an additional real-time intent: 'nurse-triage-urgent' that will be called from live web sessions. This one is high-priority and we'd like a tighter latency target if possible (thinking 95th <= 150 ms). How disruptive is that to the plan?

2) We can deliver the anonymized sample set (~6k events) by 2027-02-05; we’ll flag the urgent intent examples in a separate file.

3) We understand adding the real-time path may need different infra; please advise any cost or timeline implications. We are open to a short extension if it means shipping a more representative trial.

Also looping Maya from security tomorrow if they want to confirm docs.

—Jordan

Subject: RE: Fwd: Follow-up: POC plan & acceptance criteria — infra/feasibility note

Kim / Marissa — quick technical readout after a 30m sync with infra: 

Summary- We can support the additional low-latency intent, but the tightened 95th <= 150 ms SLO becomes a material constraint. Achieving that reliably end-to-end requires:
  - A dedicated small GPU instance group (NVIDIA A10/A30 class) with reduced batching for the "real-time" route
  - KV-cache warmup and a smaller context window for that route to keep token compute minimal
  - Network egress considerations (we estimate ~10-20 ms variability depending on region)

Impacts- Timeline: provisioning a dedicated pool + config + smoke tests adds ~10 business days; recommend +2 calendar weeks to the trial (so total trial length becomes 6 weeks with a mid-check at week 3).
- Cost: relative delta vs hosted trial roughly +15–25% for the trial period (estimates attached in infra-estimate.pdf).
- Work changes: we’ll need a short eval script to measure the 95th percentile on synthetic websocket-like sessions — I attached latency-eval-script.patch for the SE team to run.

Proposed acceptance criteria (rebaseline)- Conversational search: same as proposed (accuracy >= 92%)
- Real-time intent: 95th percentile inference latency <= 150 ms on the dedicated route (end-to-end test harness)
- Throughput: real-time path measured at representative concurrency (10 concurrent sessions) with 95th latency <= SLO

Owners / next steps- Ben: provision dedicated pool and smoke test (ETA 10 business days after scope sign-off)
- Marissa: update onboarding runbook and coordinate data ingestion with Tidal (Marissa owner for sample data validation)
- Kim: confirm timeline and update mutual action plan with Jordan

I’ll stand up the smoke test this week if we get a green light.

—Ben

  * Real-time intent (dedicated route): 95th percentile end-to-end latency <= 150 ms (measured via the provided eval harness)
  * Throughput: maintain representative concurrency targets; real-time path tested at 10 concurrent sessions
  * No more than 2% regression vs baseline on false-positive routing
- Timeline: extend trial by 2 calendar weeks (new total 6 weeks). Provisioning for dedicated pool to begin within 10 business days after signed agreement.
- Costs/credits: estimated delta +20% for trial provisioning — we can discuss a modest trial credit to offset (I’ll loop finance if needed).

- Marissa: validate sample data and run initial eval by 2027-02-18 (Marissa)
